findings.claim: The rebuilt-hash rule tries only two readings (every boundary a blank line, or every boundary nothing), so an observation whose parts mix a blank-line boundary with a mid-word cut (short paragraph S then long paragraph L split into [S],[L1],[L2]) gets no hash a hand mirror could match; the hand mirror bridges to nothing and a duplicate page can be written. False negative, not a false bridge; the base never matched multi-part observations either.
evidence: memorycard import.go:355-367 splitBody flushes, then appends cutRunes pieces of an over-long paragraph, so boundary kinds are chosen per boundary.
observations.go:72-85 applies one separator from {"\n\n",""} to every boundary; neither reading equals S + blank line + L1+L2.
CardContentHash collapses whitespace but cannot repair a missing or spurious word break.

findings.claim: Batching is correct, but every listing and every ByID for an unmapped memory reads the title and body of every imported memory of the project, including the single-id paths of the MCP promote tool and promote --source memorycard.
evidence: observations.go:37 selects m.body for every engram import_map row of the project.
ByID (source.go:49-63) goes through mapAll and kinOf.
Read observations.go, source.go at the branch tip, L46, memorycard import.go (recordParts, splitBody, cutRunes, importRow) and memory.CardContentHash.
No false bridge found: parts carry distinct (part i/n) titles; identical observations share one memory and dedupe by observation id.
